ownership.notes: Delaware corporation (CIK 1858681; formerly Tango Holdings, Inc.), the holding company since the 1 January 2022 merger with Athene Holding Ltd., now its subsidiary; fiscal year ends 31 December. APOS on the NYSE is the company's 7.625% junior subordinated notes due 2053, not common equity; its 6.75% Series A mandatory convertible preferred converted to common on 31 July 2026. Marc Rowan is Chair and Chief Executive Officer.

summary:
**BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:** Apollo signs for no power equipment itself. It reaches AI infrastructure through three channels. The first is **Stream Data Centers**, a hyperscale developer its funds have controlled since 3 November 2025, with more than 4 GW of long-term powered land. The second is a **compute-financing book**: Apollo leads the USD 35bn initial tranche of Broadcom's AI XPV Platform, which buys compute racks for Anthropic, and led a USD 3.5bn financing for Valor's lease of NVIDIA GB200 systems to xAI. The third is **Athene's balance sheet**, which guarantees 15% of the XPV purchase obligation. Its other controlled platforms are smaller buyers: Vaultica, STACK's former European colocation business; Eagle Creek's ~700 MW of hydro (agreed October 2025); and PowerGrid Services. Hornsea 3 and the TotalEnergies Texas portfolio are 50% stakes that their partners operate.

**BACKGROUND.** Per company filings, the registrant is Apollo Global Management, Inc. (NYSE: APO; CIK 1858681), a Delaware corporation with three segments: Asset Management, Retirement Services (Athene, a subsidiary since the 1 January 2022 merger) and Principal Investing. AUM was about USD 1.05tn at 30 June 2026, of which USD 858bn was fee-generating and USD 416bn was Athene's perpetual capital. Infrastructure and Clean Transition Equity was USD 21.6bn of AUM at 31 December 2025, about 2% of the firm. FY2025 adjusted net income was USD 5.2bn, or USD 8.38 a share against Zacks' USD 7.94. Q2 2026's USD 2.11 missed Zacks' USD 2.18 despite record fee-related earnings of USD 785m. The shares closed at USD 114.02 on 2 October 2026, down 21% for the year, after the Epstein disclosures and a securities class action. Q3 2026 results are due on 3 November.
ecosystemRole: We assess Apollo as the capital segment's largest AI-compute financier and the controlling owner of one scaled data-centre developer. Its funds bought a majority of Stream Data Centers (closed 3 November 2025). Stream's management builds hyperscale campuses in Chicago, Dallas, Atlanta, Phoenix and San Antonio through joint ventures, and at Elk Grove Village, Illinois, ComEd is building a 260 MW substation for its campus. Apollo leads the initial USD 35bn of Broadcom's AI XPV Platform. Under it an Apollo-managed fund, WarehouseCo Intermediate Holdings LP, holds the obligation to buy the Broadcom-designed compute racks that Anthropic leases at Fluidstack sites. That is an obligation to buy chips, not power gear. Athene is why Apollo can lead deals of that size: per company filings it guarantees 15% of the XPV purchase obligation, and per trade press it took a sizable portion of the debt. For power-equipment sellers, Apollo is a directory to the buyers — Stream, Vaultica, Eagle Creek and PowerGrid Services — not a buyer itself.

productsAndServices.name: Data-centre platforms — Stream Data Centers and Vaultica
productsAndServices.description: Apollo-managed funds agreed on 6 August 2025 to buy a majority interest in Stream Data Centers from Stream Realty Partners and completed the purchase on 3 November 2025; Stream's management and a Principal Asset Management fund keep minority stakes, and no percentage or price is disclosed. Stream 'controls over 4 gigawatts of long-term powered land', has delivered more than 20 campuses, and delivers all projects as joint ventures; a new Apollo subsidiary took over as manager of Stream's land fund, which Apollo and Stream Realty Partners committed new capital to for 650 MW of near-term capacity in metro Chicago, Atlanta and Dallas. Separately, Apollo infrastructure funds agreed on 29 April 2025 to buy STACK Infrastructure's pan-European colocation business — seven data centres in Stockholm, Oslo, Copenhagen, Milan and Geneva — which relaunched as Vaultica Data Centers in December 2025.
highlights: Elk Grove Village, Illinois: ComEd broke ground in September 2025 on the substation for Stream's campus of more than 1.2m sq ft across three buildings, due in service in 2027; T&D World gives the substation as 260 MW
Stream's chief executive since January 2026 is Michael Lahoud; it names no procurement head and no equipment supplier on the record

Reported only: The Information said on 22–23 September 2026 that Anthropic is in early talks to lease up to 1 GW directly from Stream, with Google discussed as a possible credit guarantor; no party has announced it
Vaultica: Apollo never announced the closing; an Apollo partner sits on its board, and its chief executive is Sherif Rizkalla, formerly head of STACK's European colocation business
productsAndServices.positioning: Stream is a build-to-suit and powered-land developer for hyperscale tenants; Vaultica is an interconnected enterprise colocation operator — the opposite end of the data-centre market.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Majority equity held by Apollo-managed funds; Stream's projects are delivered through joint ventures and a land fund an Apollo subsidiary manages.
productsAndServices.roadmap: 650 MW of near-term capacity across metro Chicago, Atlanta and Dallas (August 2025 release); Elk Grove Village in service in 2027.

productsAndServices.name: AI compute financing — Broadcom AI XPV Platform, Valor Compute Infrastructure, Nscale
productsAndServices.category: Credit — asset-backed and investment-grade capital solutions
productsAndServices.description: Apollo leads 'an initial $35 billion capital solution' for Broadcom's AI XPV Platform, announced on 9 June 2026 with Blackstone's Credit & Insurance business as the other initial anchor investor and with banks. It funds the racks of Broadcom-designed accelerators that Anthropic is to deploy at Fluidstack-based sites from mid-2026, across 'a multi-year draw schedule'. Per Apollo's Q2 2026 10-Q, an Apollo-managed fund, WarehouseCo Intermediate Holdings LP, holds the purchase obligation for the compute. Athene guarantees 15% of that obligation, and a third party reimburses Athene for 35% of anything it pays. Per Broadcom's 10-Q, Broadcom backstops the customer's five-year lease obligations up to about USD 29bn undiscounted. On 7 January 2026 Apollo funds led a USD 3.5bn capital solution for Valor Compute Infrastructure's USD 5.4bn acquisition and triple-net lease of NVIDIA GB200 compute to an xAI subsidiary.
highlights: The USD 35bn is the size of the initial tranche's capital commitment — not an asset value and not Apollo's own equity; Apollo's share is undisclosed, and the platform's 'over 20GW' through 2028 is a design target
Valor Compute Infrastructure, a Valor-managed fund with NVIDIA as anchor limited partner, owns the GB200 systems; Apollo is the lead financier, not an owner

Reported only: Reuters, citing The Information, said on 9 February 2026 that Apollo was close to a roughly USD 3.4bn loan to a second vehicle buying NVIDIA chips to lease to xAI; no completion is on the record

Nscale's USD 3.36bn convertible (25 September 2026) was 'led by Third Point' and 'supported by' investors including 'funds managed by Apollo'; Nscale's S-1 does not name Apollo and no amount is disclosed

On 10 August 2026 NVIDIA signed memoranda of understanding with Apollo and five other firms to mobilise over USD 500bn of third-party capital 'over time'; they 'remain subject to execution of the final agreements'
productsAndServices.positioning: The capital comes from the liability side: Athene's demand for investment-grade assets lets Apollo commit as a principal and syndicate the rest through Apollo Capital Solutions and Atlas SP Partners, as Apollo's partner on the deal describes it.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Senior and structured debt to special-purpose lessor vehicles; a fund-held purchase obligation backed by committed financing; convertible notes.
productsAndServices.roadmap: XPV fundings 'no later than 2028' per the 10-Q; final agreements under the NVIDIA memoranda are pending.

productsAndServices.name: Infrastructure and Clean Transition Equity — power, grids and energy services
productsAndServices.description: The Apollo Infrastructure Group had USD 21.6bn of AUM at 31 December 2025 across digital infrastructure, energy transition, transport and logistics, and the clean-transition private-equity strategy. Its controlling positions are Eagle Creek Renewable Energy (about 700 MW across 85 hydro plants; acquisition agreed on 6 October 2025, closing not announced), PowerGrid Services (utility maintenance and construction, majority agreed in May 2025) and, until its sale to SLB closes, Kelvion, the heat-exchanger maker. Its largest energy cheques are non-controlling: 50% of Ørsted's 2.9 GW Hornsea 3 offshore wind farm (USD 6.5bn including half of capex; Ørsted builds and operates), a EUR 3.2bn equity commitment to a joint venture with RWE holding 25.1% of the German grid operator Amprion (RWE has operational control) and 50% of TotalEnergies' ~2 GW Texas solar-and-storage portfolio (TotalEnergies operates).
highlights: Argo Infrastructure Partners, an infrastructure manager with about USD 6bn of assets, was agreed in January 2025; Bridge Investment Group, completed on 2 September 2025, is a real-estate manager

FlexGen: Apollo affiliates' funds announced a USD 150m equity commitment in August 2021; Apollo partners Olivia Wassenaar and Trevor Mills list FlexGen board seats on Apollo's own pages; the stake is undisclosed

Kelvion: SLB agreed on 31 August 2026 to buy it from Apollo-managed funds, the majority owner, and Triton for about USD 3.4bn in cash plus about USD 0.7bn of assumed debt; closing expected in the first half of 2027
Intel Fab 34 (June 2024): 49% for USD 11bn, with Intel keeping 51% and control
productsAndServices.positioning: Weighted to co-ownership beside an operator — Ørsted, RWE, TotalEnergies, Intel — rather than to platforms Apollo runs.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Infrastructure funds, hybrid-value funds and Athene-funded structured equity.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Eagle Creek and Kelvion closings pending; Hornsea 3 under construction by Ørsted.

productsAndServices.name: Retirement Services — Athene
productsAndServices.category: Insurance — annuities and pension risk transfer
productsAndServices.description: Athene Holding Ltd. issues retirement savings products, chiefly annuities, and reinsures and takes on pension liabilities; Apollo has owned it outright since the 1 January 2022 merger. Its investment portfolio — 'primarily high-grade fixed income assets' — is managed by Apollo's asset-management arm, which advised USD 392.2bn of AUM in Athene-related accounts at 31 December 2025, and Athene supplements its capital with third-party money through the ACRA sidecars and the ADIP funds. The segment's measure is spread-related earnings, USD 3,361m in 2025 and a record USD 877m in Q2 2026.
highlights: Athene is the buyer of much of what Apollo originates: Apollo's 16 origination platforms produced USD 309bn of assets in 2025
Athora, a European insurance platform Apollo advises, reached USD 121bn of perpetual capital after buying Pension Insurance Corporation in Q1 2026
A one-time USD 1.7bn tax expense in Q1 2026 followed ACRA's revocation of its election under Bermuda's Corporate Income Tax Act 2023, and produced a first-half GAAP loss
productsAndServices.positioning: The long-dated, investment-grade liability base that funds Apollo's credit franchise and its compute financings.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Annuities sold through banks, broker-dealers and independent marketing organisations; pension-group annuities; flow and block reinsurance.

strategyRead: **(High confidence)** We assess that **Apollo is a directory of power-equipment buyers, not a door**. No Apollo entity orders batteries, medium-voltage gear or generation. The buyers are the platforms its funds control — Stream Data Centers, Vaultica, Eagle Creek and PowerGrid Services — and, on its largest energy cheques (Hornsea 3, the RWE–Amprion joint venture, the TotalEnergies Texas portfolio), the operating partner. Basis: Apollo's own releases on each deal and the partners' operating roles they describe. A seller reaches Stream's development team through Apollo's portfolio and sells to Stream.

**(High confidence)** We assess that **Apollo's distinctive AI position is on the financing side, and it rests on Athene**. It leads the USD 35bn initial tranche of Broadcom's AI XPV Platform and led the USD 3.5bn Valor–xAI financing. In both, special-purpose vehicles buy the compute, the AI lab leases it, and Apollo is lender, arranger and principal investor. The 10-Q places the XPV purchase obligation in an Apollo-managed fund and a 15% guarantee on Athene. Apollo's exposure is therefore to Anthropic's and xAI's lease payments — on XPV backstopped by Broadcom up to about USD 29bn — rather than to construction.

**(Moderate confidence)** We assess that **Stream is Apollo's one scaled buyer of data-centre power equipment, and the reported Anthropic talks would deepen it**. Stream controls more than 4 GW of powered land and is building at Elk Grove Village behind a new ComEd substation. A direct 1 GW lease to Anthropic, reported on 22–23 September but announced by no party, would make an Apollo platform a lab-direct landlord beside the Broadcom racks Apollo already finances. The judgment weakens if no lease is announced by the end of 2026.

**(Moderate confidence)** We assess that **in energy Apollo is a co-owner and recycler more than an operator**. Its largest energy commitments — Hornsea 3, Amprion through RWE, TotalEnergies' Texas portfolio, Pembina Gas Infrastructure — sit beside operators. The Kelvion sale to SLB is a sizable exit. The controlled exceptions are Eagle Creek's hydro, not yet closed on the record, and PowerGrid Services.

**(Low confidence)** We assess that **the Epstein disclosures and the redemption caps are a retail-channel risk rather than an institutional one, so far**. Q2 2026 brought record organic inflows of USD 60bn even as the shares fell 21% for the year and Apollo Debt Solutions capped repurchases for a third quarter. The judgment would fail if Q3 inflows, due on 3 November, show institutional or Athene flows slowing.

**INDICATORS TO WATCH** — *Q3 2026 results, 3 November:* inflows, Athene's spread and any update on XPV drawings. *A Stream–Anthropic lease announcement:* would confirm Judgment 3 and make Stream a lab-direct landlord. *Final agreements under the NVIDIA memoranda:* the first per-firm allocation. *Eagle Creek and Kelvion closings:* one adds a controlled generation buyer, the other completes an exit. *The Southern District of New York class action:* a motion-to-dismiss ruling.

relationships.scale: USD 35bn initial tranche; more than 1 GW of compute
relationships.note: Apollo leads the initial USD 35bn capital solution of Broadcom's AI XPV Platform, which funds the compute racks Anthropic leases at Fluidstack-based sites.
relationships.context:
Broadcom announced the platform on 9 June 2026 with Apollo and Blackstone's Credit & Insurance business as initial anchor investors. Its initial tranche, led by Apollo with banks, facilitates 'Anthropic's previously-announced capacity expansion of more than 1 gigawatt of compute infrastructure' at Fluidstack-based sites from mid-2026.

Per Apollo's Q2 2026 10-Q, an Apollo-managed fund, WarehouseCo Intermediate Holdings LP, holds the purchase obligation for the compute, and Athene guarantees 15% of it. Per Broadcom's 10-Q, Broadcom backstops the customer's five-year lease payments up to about USD 29bn. Anthropic is the lessee; Apollo is the financier.

relationships.scale: More than 1 GW at Fluidstack-based sites
relationships.note: The compute racks financed by the Apollo-led XPV tranche are deployed at Fluidstack-based sites; Fluidstack is also the counterparty the reported Anthropic–Stream lease would bypass.
relationships.context:
The joint release of 9 June 2026 says the initial USD 35bn tranche will facilitate Anthropic's more-than-1 GW expansion 'expected to deploy in Fluidstack-based sites starting in mid-2026'. The racks are bought by the Apollo-managed purchaser fund and leased to Anthropic, not to Fluidstack.

On 22–23 September 2026 The Information reported Anthropic in early talks to lease up to 1 GW directly from Apollo-controlled Stream Data Centers; no party has announced it.

relationships.note: Fellow initial anchor investor, through Blackstone's Credit & Insurance business, in Broadcom's AI XPV Platform, whose initial tranche Apollo leads.
relationships.context: Broadcom's release names Apollo and Blackstone's Credit & Insurance business as the platform's 'initial anchor investors'; Apollo's own release says Apollo funds are leading the initial USD 35bn capital solution 'in partnership with Blackstone and leading global banks'. No split between the two is disclosed. Blackstone was also one of the six firms in NVIDIA's August 2026 compute-financing memoranda.

relationships.scale: Over USD 500bn of third-party capital across six firms, 'over time'
relationships.note: One of six financiers in NVIDIA's August 2026 memoranda of understanding to build compute-financing platforms; NVIDIA is also the anchor limited partner in the Valor vehicle Apollo financed.
relationships.context:
NVIDIA's release of 10 August 2026 announced memoranda with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR to mobilise over USD 500bn of third-party capital; they 'remain subject to execution of the final agreements', and no per-firm allocation is published.

Separately, Apollo's 7 January 2026 release says NVIDIA invested in Valor Compute Infrastructure as an anchor limited partner; that vehicle bought the GB200 systems Apollo financed for lease to xAI.

relationships.scale: USD 3.5bn financing of a USD 5.4bn transaction
relationships.note: Apollo funds led a USD 3.5bn capital solution for Valor Compute Infrastructure's USD 5.4bn acquisition and lease of NVIDIA GB200 compute to an xAI subsidiary.
relationships.context:
Apollo's 7 January 2026 release: Apollo-managed funds 'led a $3.5 billion capital solution for Valor Compute Infrastructure L.P. (VCI), a fund managed by Valor Equity Partners', to support its USD 5.4bn acquisition and triple-net lease of data-centre compute infrastructure, including NVIDIA GB200 GPUs, to a subsidiary of xAI Corp. Valor's fund owns the systems; Apollo is the lead financier.

Reported only: Reuters, citing The Information, said on 9 February 2026 that Apollo was close to a roughly USD 3.4bn loan to a second chip-lease vehicle for xAI; no completion is on the record.

relationships.scale: Seven colocation data centres in five European markets
relationships.note: Apollo infrastructure funds bought STACK Infrastructure's pan-European colocation business in a carve-out agreed on 29 April 2025; it now trades as Vaultica Data Centers.
relationships.context: Apollo's release describes seven data centres in Stockholm, Oslo, Copenhagen, Milan and Geneva bought from STACK Infrastructure, 'a portfolio company of Blue Owl Digital Infrastructure Advisors LLC', and says the business would drop the STACK name. Apollo did not announce the closing; the business relaunched as Vaultica Data Centers in December 2025, and an Apollo partner lists a Vaultica board seat. STACK kept its hyperscale business.

relationships.note: Blue Owl Digital Infrastructure's portfolio company STACK was the seller in the April 2025 carve-out of its European colocation business to Apollo infrastructure funds.
relationships.context: Apollo's 29 April 2025 release names STACK Infrastructure as 'a portfolio company of Blue Owl Digital Infrastructure Advisors LLC'. The seven-site business relaunched under Apollo funds as Vaultica Data Centers in December 2025. No price was disclosed.

relationships.note: Funds managed by Apollo affiliates committed USD 150m of equity to FlexGen in 2021; two Apollo infrastructure partners list FlexGen board seats; the current stake is undisclosed.
relationships.context: The 25 August 2021 release announced a USD 150m equity commitment from funds managed by affiliates of Apollo, alongside FlexGen's existing investors. Apollo has published nothing on FlexGen since, including on FlexGen's 2025 purchase of Powin's assets, but Apollo's own leadership pages list FlexGen among the boards of Olivia Wassenaar, head of the Apollo Infrastructure Group, and Trevor Mills. No ownership percentage or control right is disclosed; it is a minority growth investment, not a controlled platform.

relationships.note: Funds managed by Apollo are among the investors 'supporting' Nscale's USD 3.36bn pre-IPO convertible, which Third Point led; the amount is undisclosed.
relationships.context: Nscale's 25 September 2026 release lists 'funds managed by Apollo' with NVIDIA, Citadel, Hudson Bay Capital, Abu Dhabi Investment Council and 8090 Industries among the supporters of a round led by Third Point. Nscale's S-1, filed 18 September, records a subscription agreement for at least USD 3.1bn (USD 2.1bn of unsecured convertible loan notes plus USD 1.0bn to NVIDIA) and does not name Apollo. Convertible notes are debt until an IPO; typed as a lender-style link.

technicalSpecs.notes: An investor passes the buying-authority test only through a platform it controls. Apollo passes through Stream, Vaultica and PowerGrid Services, and would pass through Eagle Creek on closing. It fails on every 50% energy stake, where the partner builds and operates, and on the compute vehicles, where it is the lender. No Apollo platform has a named power-equipment supplier on the record.
